requirement.text: The system shall be easy to use

classification.rationale: Neither the target requirement nor the surrounding document context contains specific indicators for web, mobile, or AI systems; it describes generic usability and maintainability qualities.

rounds.text_checked: The system shall be easy to use

issues.explanation: The phrase 'easy to use' is a vague quality attribute with no quantifiable or measurable threshold.

questions.question_text: What specific, measurable usability criteria or metrics (such as task completion time, maximum training duration, or target success rate) should be used to define 'easy to use' for requirement PURE-GAMMA-J-0033?

answers.answer_text: No document-defined threshold exists. Proposing: a new user completes the core purchase flow (browse to checkout) without assistance in under 5 minutes, and the interface achieves a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of at least 70 in usability testing.

test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence Partitioning and Boundary Value Analysis apply because the requirement specifies numeric thresholds (under 5 minutes completion time, SUS score of at least 70). Performance applies due to the explicit timing constraint requiring the flow to be completed in under 5 minutes. Use Case applies because the requirement describes a multi-step user scenario (the core purchase flow from browse to checkout).

test_cases.title: Unassisted New User Core Purchase Flow Completion
test_cases.preconditions: A new user with no prior training or exposure to the system is provided access to the product store homepage.
steps: Instruct the new user to select a product and purchase it without providing any guidance or assistance.
Observe the user browsing the catalog and selecting a product.
Observe the user adding the item to the shopping cart and proceeding to checkout.
Observe the user entering shipping address, selecting payment method, and placing the order.
test_cases.expected_result: The new user successfully completes the entire purchase flow from browsing to order placement without requesting or receiving assistance.

test_cases.title: Core Purchase Flow Time Measurement - Under 5 Minutes
test_cases.preconditions: Timing instrumentation is active. The new user is placed on the homepage.
steps: Start high-precision timer as the new user begins browsing on the homepage.
User navigates to product page, adds item to cart, proceeds to checkout, inputs checkout details, and clicks submit.
Stop timer immediately upon loading of the order confirmation page.
test_cases.expected_result: Total elapsed time from starting search/browse to displaying the final order confirmation page is strictly under 300 seconds (5 minutes).

test_cases.title: System Usability Scale Score Threshold Verification (SUS >= 70)
test_cases.preconditions: A formal usability study panel of representative new users completes the purchase flow.
steps: Administer standard 10-question System Usability Scale (SUS) survey immediately after each new user completes the flow.
Calculate normalized SUS score (0-100 scale) for each participant.
Compute the mean SUS score across all test participants.
Compare mean score against boundary conditions (69 = Fail, 70 = Pass).
test_cases.expected_result: The calculated mean System Usability Scale score across participants is equal to or greater than 70.

test_cases.title: Equivalence Partitioning for Purchase Completion Time and SUS Score
test_cases.preconditions: Usability test data recorded across multiple user cohorts.
steps: Evaluate test session duration class 1 (Valid: < 300 seconds).
Evaluate test session duration class 2 (Invalid: >= 300 seconds).
test_cases.expected_result: Sessions falling in Valid partitions (< 300 seconds completion time and SUS score >= 70) meet the usability requirement, while sessions in Invalid partitions are flagged as non-compliant.

final_text: The system shall allow a new user to complete the core purchase flow (browse to checkout) without assistance in under 5 minutes and achieve a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of at least 70 in usability testing.
